accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS Mathematics 2.MD.6 (whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line with equally spaced points; sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram), DfE NC 2013 Year 2 and Year 3 number and mental-method statements, and NCETM Year 2 number line guidance. Every lab answer was recomputed: ribbons 4, 7, 9 cover that many unit spaces and touch one more tick; 36, 43, 48 lie on the 30-50 line; 38 + 27 = 65, 46 + 35 = 81, 59 + 24 = 83, 72 - 35 = 37, 64 - 28 = 36, 91 - 46 = 45; robot lines 45 + 30 = 75 and 50 - 20 = 30. Parameterised items a+20+b (21..49, 1..9 stays within 100 at every corner), a-30 (41..99 stays positive) and ribbon lengths are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented number-line errors in Bobis (2007) and Teppo and van den Heuvel-Panhuizen (2014): counting tick marks instead of intervals (ribbon predict, n+1 ribbon feedback, robot line 1, m2, m3, challenge 'tick'), starting the count at 1 (ribbon feedback, m7, challenge 'start'), landing in the wrong ten or one space off when only tens are labelled (spot feedback for +/-10 and +/-1, p3, m6, challenge 'ten'), jumping right to subtract (back-jump predict, the +10 decoy tile in the take-away scene, robot line 3, p4, m9, challenge 'dir') and unequal spacing (robot line 4, p5, challenge 'equal').

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about intervals and jumps on a scaled line: a ribbon measured in unit spaces, an arrow dragged to a value between labelled tens, a frog whose arcs must total the second addend exactly (overshoot is refused with the excess named), and take-away jumps that refuse a rightward tile. flagnline estimates positions on 0-100 and 0-1000 and flagcounton counts on in ones along a track; neither measures lengths as spaces or builds tens-and-ones jump strings. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_numlen.js under 30% similarity to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule before the text gives it: an n+1 answer to the ribbon gets the tick-versus-space message, the arrow scene only labels tens so the child has to find the ten and count spaces, and the jump scenes show a running 'jumped x of b' total so the child sees that 2 tens and 7 ones make 27 and why the frog lands on 65. Step summaries confirm each rule after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Ribbon predict offers '5, one for each tick' against '4, one for each space'; the scene then shows the 5 ticks and the 4 numbered spaces. Take-away predict offers 'Right, away from 0' against 'Left, back towards 0'; the scene has a +10 tile that is refused with the direction rule. Both wrong options are the documented mistakes, and the reveal names the prediction the child made.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each with two tagged wrong answers. why() has seven distinct messages: tick (counted marks), start (started at 1), dir (jumped the wrong way), ten (wrong ten), one (moved ones not tens), once (only one jump of 10 for 30) and equal (unequal spaces). Each names the slip and the fix, with numbers from the question.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and the words space, mark, jump, right, left; validate_lessons passes the family kid target (FK grade 5.0 + 0.5) and adult target. Curriculum terms for adults: number line, tick mark, interval, equal spaces, jump, difference, and the standard code 2.MD.6. Lab banners are under 12 words and shrink to fit at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph gives a rule with a worked example (ribbon 0 to 4, 38 + 27, 72 - 35). The adult text gives the year and standard, the key words, the tick-counting mistake and the start-at-1 slip with a fix, the wrong-ten and wrong-direction slips, and what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrase and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 x 1000 phone screenshots of the canvas in light and dark themes for all six steps before and after Show me: number keys are two rows of five tiles about 58 px wide, jump tiles fit in one row of four or five, the 30-50 and 30-70 lines keep labels at each ten without overlap, banners shrink to one line, and the robot's Right and Slip buttons sit inside the canvas. A scripted check found no visible lab button under 44 x 44 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin under the canvas: 'The ribbon is 7 long', arrow moves of 1 and 10 plus 'Put the arrow on 43', each jump tile and Undo, and Right or Slip. The canvas aria-label is updated with every message, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13. Canvas colours switch to lighter shades in the dark theme so the pink ribbon, blue arcs and green frog labels keep contrast.
